record.context_brief: Free regular bands in semigroup rings
record.original_question: If B is the free left regular band or free right regular band on generators x1, x2, ..., xn, what is the detailed structure of the skew lattice generated by B inside the semigroup ring Z(B)?

evidence.quote: If B is the free left (right) regular band on generators, x1 , x2 , . . . , xn , what must its generated skew lattice in Z(B) look like. . . in detail?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A band is a semigroup $(B,\cdot)$ in which every element is idempotent, i.e. $x\cdot x = x$ for all $x\in B$. A band $B$ is called a left regular band if it satisfies the identity $x\cdot y\cdot x = x\cdot y$ for all $x,y\in B$; it is called a right regular band if it satisfies $x\cdot y\cdot x = y\cdot x$ for all $x,y\in B$. For a fixed integer $n\ge 1$, let $B$ denote the free left regular band (respectively, the free right regular band) on the generators $x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n$.

Consider the integral semigroup ring $\mathbb{Z}(B) = \mathbb{Z}[B]$, whose elements are finite $\mathbb{Z}$-linear combinations of elements of $B$ and whose multiplication extends that of $B$ by linearity. Define on $\mathbb{Z}(B)$ the operation
$$ a\wedge b := a\cdot b,\qquad a\vee b := a + b - a\cdot b\quad\text{(or its right-handed analogue)}, $$
and let $\mathbf{S}(B)$ be the smallest subset of $\mathbb{Z}(B)$ that contains $B$ and is closed under both $\wedge$ and $\vee$. A skew lattice is an algebra $(S,\wedge,\vee)$ such that $\wedge$ and $\vee$ are each associative and idempotent and satisfy the absorption identities
$$ x\wedge(x\vee y)=x=x\vee(x\wedge y),\qquad (x\wedge y)\vee y = y = (x\vee y)\wedge y. $$
The set $\mathbf{S}(B)$ forms a skew lattice under $(\wedge,\vee)$, called the skew lattice generated by $B$ inside $\mathbb{Z}(B)$.

Problem: Describe explicitly and in detail the structure of the skew lattice $\mathbf{S}(B)$. In particular, give a presentation or canonical form for its elements; determine its $\mathcal{D}$-class decomposition and the structure of each $\mathcal{D}$-class; describe its maximal lattice image; describe the natural partial order; and give its cardinality (or growth in $n$) when finite, or a description of its elements when infinite.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any published explicit structural description of the skew lattice generated inside $\mathbb{Z}(B)$ by the free left/right regular band on $n$ generators. Related work concerns the semigroup algebra and quiver of left regular bands and general theory of skew lattices in rings, but the specific detailed structure asked for does not appear to have been worked out, suggesting the problem remains open.

status_evidence.snippet: Studies the semigroup algebra of a left regular band and its quiver, but does not address the generated skew lattice in detail.
status_evidence.claim: Related research addresses semigroup algebras of left regular bands without describing the generated skew lattice.
